186: ✦Food still moves slowly through your digestive system, and the growing uterus keeps pressing on your intestines. As a result you may continue to have heartburn or constipation.
187: ✦Vaginal discharge may increase.✦If it's thin, white and odourless or mild-smelling, there's nothing to worry about.
188: ✦Vitamin A: this vitamin is essential for human reproduction.✦It strengthens the immune system.✦Vitamin A is found in milk, egg yolk, butter, leafy greens, citrus, apricots, broccoli, kale, carrots, peaches, spinach, potatoes, pumpkin and Brussels sprouts.✦These food sources of vitamin A are fine during pregnancy (avoid high-dose supplements unless your doctor advises them).✦A lack of vitamin A weakens the immune system.✦A weaker immune system raises the risk of infections.✦Since vitamin A is important for the embryo's development, a deficiency may cause developmental problems.
189: ✦You may have heartburn at this stage.✦It happens when stomach acid is pushed up into the oesophagus. As your baby grows, there's less room for your organs.✦This squeeze causes heartburn.
190: ✦As you enter the last trimester, your baby is developing quickly.✦The kicks and movements have become stronger.✦Your body is adapting to your baby, bringing many aches and pains.✦Staying active in daily life can help you cope with the changes.✦If your sleep is disrupted, take more frequent naps during the day.
191: ✦If you started pregnancy at a normal weight, gaining 11 to 14 kg in total is ideal.✦At 28 weeks, weight is expected to increase by about 500–700 grams a week.✦So far you may have gained a total of 7.7–10.8 kg.
192: ✦Around this time some mothers-to-be feel an uncomfortable crawling sensation in their lower legs.✦Because it's uncomfortable, it makes it hard to keep the legs still.✦If the sensation goes away when you move your legs, you may have restless legs syndrome.
193: ✦Fear of labour, negative birth stories heard from others and negative accounts of one's own birth are among the main causes of fear of childbirth.✦This creates a kind of 'negative hypnosis', so the mother-to-be – and even the father-to-be – may fear vaginal birth.
194: ✦Another factor is limited experience with normal birth among some doctors, and not giving enough room to midwives, whose profession is attending births (obstetricians train in managing complications, while midwives train for years specifically in supporting birth).
195: ✦Birth is a natural process that many women can go through without medication.✦Considering all of this, what matters most is that the mother doesn't have a traumatic birth experience.✦Mothers, doctors and midwives should all aim for this above all.✦So the first thing mothers who want a vaginal birth should do is take a birth preparation class.✦Doctors and midwives should also guide mothers-to-be to these classes.✦Another important point is choosing a doctor who knows natural birth practices and has a high rate of normal births, or one who will respect and support all your birth preferences.
196: ✦At 28 weeks, production of colostrum, the first milk, may begin.✦But don't express it.✦Doing so may trigger early labour.
197: ✦If there's a blood type incompatibility (Rh), you may need to repeat the indirect Coombs test at 28 weeks.✦Watch out for rising blood pressure.✦Remember that high blood pressure is risky for both baby and mother.
198: ✦Your belly is growing fast. Aching joints, heartburn and frequent trips to the toilet can affect your sleep. Lying on your left side helps your circulation, digestion, lungs and kidneys work more easily. You can also support your body with a few pillows. For example, a pillow between your legs will relieve your hips and lower back.
199: ✦If you prefer to sleep on your back, raise your left side slightly with a pillow.✦This eases pressure on the vena cava, the vein that carries blood from your lower body to your heart.
200: ✦You may need the toilet several times a night.✦So drink the recommended 2 litres earlier in the day and go to the toilet before bed.
201: ✦Heartburn and constipation continue.✦The hormone progesterone relaxes your muscles, so digestion slows down.✦Slow digestion and a crowded belly cause gas and heartburn.✦Especially if you eat large meals.✦Eating small, frequent meals may make you more comfortable.
202: ✦You may now feel weary of waiting.✦You may want the pregnancy to end as soon as possible.✦Or you may have worries about the baby.✦These can show up as nightmares.✦There's no reason to feel your nightmares will come true.✦They're a reflection of your fears and worries – a way of coping with them.
203: ✦In pregnancy, prolactin rises in your body, preparing your breasts to make milk.✦Colostrum, the baby's first milk, has already started forming.✦It may even leak from your breasts sometimes.✦Don't panic – wear breast pads now and then so your clothes don't get stained.
204: ✦As the baby grows this week, your internal organs shift.✦Your stomach and intestines are pushed upward.✦The uterine muscles are strong enough to keep your organs from being harmed.✦This squeeze on your stomach and intestines is the main cause of indigestion.
205: ✦During pregnancy your baby takes all the nutrients they need from you.✦If you don't eat enough, your baby will use your reserves and you may feel tired and weak.✦In the last 3 months, weight gain is typically about 0.5 kg a week (ask your doctor what's right for you).✦This may decrease in the final weeks.✦In the last 3 months your daily calorie intake can be about 450–500 calories more than before pregnancy.✦In the final weeks, eating small and often is helpful.✦Choose nutrient-rich foods over sugary, high-calorie ones.✦Keep drinking at least 8–10 glasses of fluid a day as usual.
206: ✦Watching your diet isn't enough to stay fit.✦Keep up the exercises you've agreed with your doctor.✦In the final weeks you can reduce their pace and duration.✦Don't skip pelvic floor exercises.✦To do them, squeeze and relax the muscles around your vagina, urethra and anus.✦Hold each squeeze for 10 seconds.✦Rest between and repeat 10 times.✦Then do 10 quick squeezes of 1 second each.✦After that, squeeze and release the vaginal, urinary and anal muscles separately.✦You can also practise while urinating:✦Stop the flow and release it.✦Then finish urinating (don't do this regularly – just to find the right muscles).
207: ✦You may feel a bit tired these days, especially if you're having trouble sleeping.✦You may even lose your balance now and then.✦With your baby growing, you're heavier.✦Hormonal changes have also loosened your ligaments, leaving the joints that support your balance weaker.
208: ✦Your mood swings continue.✦Uncomfortable symptoms and hormonal changes cause emotional ups and downs.
209: ✦You may have started worrying about how the birth will go or what kind of parent you'll be.✦If you're finding these feelings hard to handle, or your anxiety and restlessness are increasing, talk to your doctor.
210: ✦In this final stage you may have urinary problems.✦In particular, cystitis – with a burning feeling when urinating – may occur.✦If you think you have a urinary tract infection, see your doctor without delay.✦Drinking plenty of water and going to the toilet whenever you need to are important for clearing infection.
211: ✦Many women wonder whether taking a bath is safe for the baby late in pregnancy.✦Most doctors agree that bathing in pregnancy is safe.✦Just be careful getting in and out of the tub and make sure the water isn't too hot.
212: ✦From this week your belly will grow surprisingly fast each week.✦It's best not to compare your bump with other mothers-to-be at the same stage.✦If people comment, just tune them out.✦Every woman's body type is different.✦So bump sizes and shapes vary in pregnancy.✦The size of your bump doesn't show whether you'll have a big or small baby.✦If something worries you, talk to your doctor.
213: ✦From this week you can start discussing your birth preferences with your doctor.✦You can ask whether they work with a midwife who can give you one-to-one support during labour.✦Supporting birth is the midwife's area of expertise.✦If one-to-one midwife support isn't available, you can arrange a doula (birth companion) to encourage you during labour and guide you on baby care before and after birth.✦You could also choose a midwife with additional doula training.✦Either can help make your birth experience healthy and positive.
214: ✦You may feel false contractions (Braxton Hicks) in these weeks.✦These contractions, which can start after weeks 20–21, are the body's rehearsal for birth.✦They exercise the muscles the uterus will use to push the baby out.✦They start at the top and move down, lasting 30 seconds to 2 minutes.✦If they bother you, rest, or walk around, drink some water or do something else to take your mind off them.✦In the last months they may get stronger and worry the mother-to-be.✦If contractions become frequent and regular, contact your doctor without delay.
215: ✦You may have noticed colostrum (first milk) leaking from your breasts.✦If so, try tucking nursing pads into your bra to protect your clothes.✦If your bra feels too tight, get a nursing bra.✦Choose one a size larger than your usual bra.
216: ✦Feeling out of breath is common at this stage, but shortness of breath can also be a sign of anaemia.✦Anaemia is caused by a lack of iron.✦It's more common during pregnancy.✦That's because your blood has much more fluid diluting your red blood cells.✦Anaemia can usually be treated easily by adding iron-rich foods and supplements to your diet.✦If you're worried, talk to your doctor.
217: ✦Wearing rings or a watch can cause circulation problems. A ring may become too tight and impossible to remove. If you have swelling, take a break from jewellery and accessories that bother you.
218: ✦After preparing poultry or dishes with raw eggs, clean counters, utensils, plates and pans with hot soapy water and disinfectant.✦Cook poultry thoroughly.✦Don't eat foods made with raw eggs.✦Don't taste anything containing raw egg before it's cooked.✦Cook eggs thoroughly.✦Boil eggs for at least 7 minutes.✦Avoid eggs fried sunny side up with runny yolks.
219: ✦This week the top of your uterus (fundus) is about 4–5 cm above your belly button.✦As it stretches your ribs and squeezes your organs, you may feel short of breath and have heartburn and indigestion.
220: ✦As your growing uterus presses on your stomach, you may feel less like overeating.✦Eating small and often helps prevent reflux.✦Your baby's organ development is complete.✦The lungs are in the final stages of development.✦So if the baby is born this week, the chance of survival is very high.✦They'll only need help with breathing for about 4 weeks.
221: ✦This week your growing belly may wake you often at night.✦So you may feel tired and irritable.✦Take more frequent rest breaks at this stage of pregnancy.✦Sleep whenever you get the chance.✦Positions to avoid when sleeping are on your back and, ideally, on your right side.✦Lying on your back can press on the main vein returning blood to the heart.✦Lying on your right side may also affect circulation through the large vein on that side.✦Not enough blood reaching the heart is risky for mother and baby.✦The healthiest position is on your left side.✦Lying on your left keeps your circulation healthy and also benefits your baby's circulation.✦It sends more blood to the placenta, helps your digestive system work well and helps you sleep more comfortably.✦When lying on your left side, support your back with a few pillows to ease back pain.✦This also stops you rolling onto your back without noticing while you sleep.
222: ✦If frequent night-time trips to the toilet disturb your sleep, avoid drinking in the evening.✦Don't think about worrying things before bed.✦Share what's bothering you with your partner in the evening and let it go.✦Sleeping on a high pillow or a few stacked pillows can prevent reflux at night.✦Do prenatal yoga before bed.✦Meditating after yoga helps you sleep deeply and calmly.
223: ✦Now and then you may feel your uterine muscles tighten.✦Many women feel these mild, false contractions, known as Braxton Hicks, as birth approaches.✦Especially in a second pregnancy.✦They're more frequent when you don't drink enough, so be sure to drink plenty of fluids.✦Your blood volume has increased by 40–50% to meet your and your baby's needs.✦Because your uterus presses on your diaphragm, you may have heartburn and shortness of breath.
224: ✦Sciatica is also a common complaint at this stage.✦It usually happens when your baby's position presses on your sciatic nerve.✦As a result you may feel sharp pain in your lower back and legs.✦Try sitting cross-legged on the floor or using an exercise ball instead of a chair.
225: ✦If sitting is painful, support your lower back with a cushion.✦Sleeping on your left side may help.✦To ease pain, apply hot or cold compresses to your back.✦If you lie on your back, a pillow under your lower back may be relieving.
226: ✦As your baby grows, you may start moving differently.✦For example, where you used to stroll, you may now waddle.
227: ✦Never mind sleeping – you may struggle even to find a comfortable sitting position.✦You may keep bumping into things at home or outside.✦This is perfectly normal.✦You may feel pain and numbness in your fingers, wrists and hands.✦Like all your other tissues, your wrists can retain water, increasing pressure in the carpal tunnel.✦When the nerves in this channel are compressed, they can cause numbness, tingling, aching, burning or sharp pain.
228: ✦Try a wrist splint to keep your wrist straight, or raise your arm on a pillow while sleeping.✦If your work involves repetitive hand movements (such as typing), remember to stretch your hands often.
229: ✦Middle-of-the-night dashes to the toilet, leg cramps, heartburn and a basketball-sized belly will certainly make sleep harder.✦Insomnia at this stage affects about three-quarters of women.✦It can also come from worries about the upcoming birth and things to do before the baby arrives.
230: ✦This week your body needs rest.✦So worrying or counting the minutes won't help.✦Pregnancy insomnia is actually great practice for the sleepless nights ahead.
231: ✦You and your baby are both growing.✦You need more energy now.✦The quality of your food matters more than the quantity.✦Key nutrients at this stage include vitamin D, iron and omega-3 fatty acids such as DHA.
232: ✦Since your fast-growing baby leaves little room for your stomach, heartburn may be more of a problem now.✦You may find several small meals a day more comfortable than three big ones.
